note: 'through His Spirit in your inner being' -- the Spirit of the Father named in verse 14, read as the Holy Spirit.

The third passage this type rests on, and the one that is not a formula. Ephesians 3:14-19 is a single sentence naming 'the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ' (v14), 'His Spirit' (v16), 'so that Christ may dwell in your hearts' (v17) and 'the fullness of God' (v19). Unlike the two formulas it also states a relation between them -- the Father grants, by the Spirit, so that Christ may dwell -- and what that relation implies is left where the corpus leaves it. Marked implied because verse 16 says 'His Spirit' rather than naming the Holy Spirit: the reading is standard and it is a reading.; 'He will glorify Me by taking from what is Mine' (16:14), with the Father named in the next verse. Implied because 16:13-15 says 'the Spirit of truth' rather than the Holy Spirit.; Named together at Matthew 28:19 -- 'in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit' -- and at 2 Corinthians 13:14. Also at 1 John 5:7 in the KJV only; see [[the_three_named_together]] for its textual status.
